title: Route Inspector — Keystroke Mapping & Locale-aware Number Formatting Prototype
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need a focused accessibility and localization pass for the new 'Route Inspector' panel used on cost and rollout pages. The panel surfaces route-level token breakdowns, actionable filters, and a compact timeline scrubber. This ticket covers the prototype review that pairs keyboard-first navigation (keystroke mappings and focus traps) with locale-aware number formatting and dynamic density adjustments for high-contrast and large-text modes. Goal: ship a developer-friendly, WCAG-compliant Route Inspector that reads cleanly with screen readers and formats currency/units correctly for regional settings.
acceptance_criteria: All interactive controls in Route Inspector reachable and operable using keyboard only (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrow keys, and single-key shortcuts documented)
Focus order is logical across route list, filters, timeline scrubber and detail pane; focus trap present when inspector is modal-like
Visible focus indicators meet contrast and minimum size requirements for high-density and compact modes
Number formatting honors user locale from Console settings and falls back to browser locale for currency, thousands separator, and decimal places
Screen reader announces the selected route, its aggregate cost, and the active filter context succinctly (1–2 lines), with ARIA live region for updates
Prototype passes a small audit with 3 external testers (NVDA/VoiceOver/JAWS) and two locales (en-US, de-DE)
Design handoff includes interaction spec, keystroke map, and a small component token matrix for contrast/size variants
design_notes: Introduce an explicit keystroke map accessible from the inspector header (hotkey '?' opens overlay) — map must show single-key shortcuts for quick route switching
Use an affordance for locale indicator next to the cost summary; clicking cycles display formats (auto / locale / engineering units)
Prefer explicit ARIA roles for the scrubber (role='slider') with aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext that contains localized time or token counts
Compact density reduces padding but preserves 48px hit target where possible; use an overlay focus ring in compact mode to keep contrast without reshaping layout
Color tokens: primary accent (token selection) needs 4.5:1 contrast against both default and high-contrast backgrounds; fallback palette provided in token matrix
accessibility_checks: Keyboard nav: full coverage test plan with key sequence table and expected focus landing spots
Screen reader: announce concise summary with ARIA live polite updates, ensure repeated updates are throttled
Contrast: test tokens at 100%, 75%, 50% opacity over light/dark surfaces with WCAG AA target (4.5:1) — list failing pairs in handoff
Hit targets: confirm tap/click areas meet 44px minimum on mobile breakpoints
High-contrast mode: provide forced high-contrast style overrides; test on Windows high-contrast themes
localization_checks: Number & currency formatting: use Intl.NumberFormat with locale fallback; confirm currencies show symbol and localized grouping
Right-to-left readiness: inspect flow when Console locale is 'ar' — ensure scrubber and timeline mirroring works
Pluralization: route count labels should be handled via ICU messages not string concatenation
Truncation & wrapping: long route names should use accessible tooltips (aria-label) and not rely solely on ellipses
Keyboard labels: short single-key shortcuts must not conflict with browser or screen reader modifiers in localized layouts
